newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen on growth path next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen on growth path next week.

text.p: The Polish bourse should extend its current downward correction early next week but analysts said enough stocks were attractively priced for shares to return to an upward path by the middle of the week.
They said gains should not prove as large as during the recent six-session 14.5-percent surge led by large-cap banks but that rises by industrials could lead the slower growth.

"Firms in the construction, power and furniture industries which are gaining from the recent flooding are a lot cheaper than comparable firms in Hungary or Russia," said Dariusz Piszczatowski of Polish Development Bank (PBR) house.
The main market' all-share WIG index rose one percent this week to 16,920.4 points, bouyed by Monday's 3.3 percent rise which had lifted the main index above 17,000.
The bourse closes on Friday for the Assumption holiday.
Analysts said the current downward correction would likely not send the index below 16,500 points.

They said macroeconomic indicators were generally good, reflected by a government analyst's Wednesday comment that 1997 GDP may grow 5.7 percent and inflation stay at the forecast 13 percent despite the recent floods.

But the analyst, Zbigniew Kuzmiuk, said the current account gap was seen widening to $6.5 billion or five percent of gross doemstic product in 1997 against a $1.35 billion or one percent of GDP deficit in 1996.
"Aside from the current account figure there's nothing macroeconomic that should lower demand on the bourse," said Janusz Oleksiak, an analyst at Bank Slaski brokerage.
More economic clues will be available next week when the July inflation figure is released on Monday followed by PPI data and construction and industrial output on Tuesday.
Analysts said the relative weak link between the Polish and U.S. bourses would limit Poland's exposure to any sharp price swings on the Dow from the U.S.'s current economic data wave.

Analysts said Tuesday's news the co-ruling Peasant Party (PSL) would seek to dismiss the prime minister over farm policy could be seen as electioneering ahead of the September 21 parliamentary vote and have no significant effect on shares.
But they said the election run-up in general could help keep the bourse below 18,000 points in coming weeks.
This week's biggest loser on the main market, ZEW, plunged 30.7 percent upon resuming trade after a month-long suspension due to flooding but analysts said the electrode maker should soon bottom out.
